title: Tenant-aware stress replay and autoscaler safety protocol
creator: Priya Nair
description: Build a tenant-aware load replay harness and an associated acceptance protocol that validates dedicated capacity throughput guarantees and autoscaler safety for customer-facing signoffs. The harness must replay realistic per-tenant mixes (QPS, prompt length distribution, cache-prefix reuse) and exercise autoscaler policies (scale-up heuristics, cooldowns, burst/buffer capacity) under controlled network and noisy-neighbor perturbations. Deliverables: (1) an extensible replay tool that produces reproducible runs and SLO-aligned metrics, (2) a standard benchmark methodology and dataset of 'golden workload signatures', (3) an acceptance checklist and runbook for customer validation and signoff. This ticket scopes the engineering work to implement the harness, the telemetry hooks, and the automated acceptance checks for rollout to the Dedicated onboarding flow.
acceptance_criteria: Replay harness can ingest a tenant workload signature (JSON) and produce a deterministic 6-hour stress run with identical seed results repeatable within a +/-10% tolerance for p50/p95/p99 latencies and token throughput.

Autoscaler safety scenarios: in aggressive, balanced, and conservative policy presets the harness demonstrates no uncontrolled oscillation (no >2 scale events per minute sustained) and never violates the configured customer SLO (p99 latency) for >5 minutes during steady-state for the golden workloads.
Harness emits per-tenant metrics (qps, tokens/sec, p50/p95/p99, kv-cache hit rate, batch size distribution, GPU utilization) to our metrics backend and a pre-built dashboard template is available.
Provides a customer acceptance checklist and signed-off run report template with pass/fail gates that the Solutions/Success team can use for onboarding Dedicated customers.
End-to-end runs instrumented with network fault injection and noisy-neighbor CPU/GPU contention, and documented mitigation notes when SLO gaps are observed.
implementation_notes: Build on top of the existing prober library but replace the single-tenant driver with a tenant-mixer that models multiple tenant buckets, per-tenant token length histograms, and KV cache locality semantics.

Replay format: canonical JSON 'workload-signature' describing temporal QPS curve, prompt-length CDF, model variant, and expected cache prefix similarity; include a seed field for deterministic pseudo-random sampling.
Execution: Kubernetes Job/StatefulSet variant that can be scaled to produce sustained load and a lightweight controller to coordinate step changes (ramp, sustain, spike).
Telemetry: push metrics via Prometheus exporter and structured traces to the APM pipeline. Add labels: tenant_id_stub, policy_preset, run_id, perturbation_tag.
Autoscaler hooks: instrument the autoscaler API to emit decision events (reason, target_replicas, observed_utilization) so replay can validate policy behavior and cooldown enforcement.
Cost-safety: include a dry-run mode that computes estimated GPU-hours and cost delta for a run without executing against production fleets.
Security: avoid using real customer data. All 'tenant' signatures used for acceptance must be anonymized or synthetic; document how to generate representative signatures from aggregated telemetry.
testing_plan: Phase 1 (dev): unit tests for workload-signature parser + deterministic RNG; small kubernetes smoke runs against a local dev cluster.
Phase 2 (staging): run golden workloads against a staging dedicated cluster; compare metric deltas to historical production baselines and tune sampling seeds until within acceptance tolerances.

Phase 3 (safety): run the three autoscaler presets with injected network jitter, increased GC pauses, and a noisy-neighbor GPU hog process to validate safe scaling behavior and identify fallback thresholds.

Phase 4 (customer acceptance kit): produce an automated run report and example signoff flow; coordinate a 2-hour joint run with Solutions Engineering and the first pilot customer for on-premises validation.
Regression: add harness runs to the nightly throughput verification pipeline for any change to autoscaler code or runtime kernel selection logic.
